findings.summary: Timezone fix misses date/time ARRAY OIDs — timestamp[]/date[] are still parsed into JS Dates shifted by the Node runtime timezone
findings.evidence: RAW_TEXT_OIDS only contains the scalar OIDs DATE (1082), TIMESTAMP (1114) and TIMESTAMPTZ (1184). The corresponding array OIDs (_date 1182, _timestamp 1115, _timestamptz 1185) are not listed, so `getDefaultParser` returns pg-types' array parser which delegates to the same date parser the comment says is broken. A query returning `timestamp[]` therefore still yields Date objects built with the Node process timezone; `toCell` then JSON.stringifies them and the rendered cell shows an instant offset by the server TZ — exactly the bug this change is meant to fix, just one level of nesting away. Same applies to composite/row and range types containing timestamps.

findings.summary: Leftover duplicate test: 'queries real tables with rows' now exists twice with conflicting expectations on the same table
findings.evidence: The diff adds a new `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` (around line 115+) while the pre-existing one at line 309 remains verbatim. Both create/populate/drop the same `_test_products` table in the shared Prisma database, and the old copy still asserts the pre-change row shape (`expect(dataResult.rows).toEqual([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }, ...])`, line 370). The author almost certainly meant to replace the old test, not duplicate it; the duplicate doubles runtime and makes the two assertions drift silently.

findings.summary: New e2e test's DROP TABLE cleanup is not in a finally — a failed assertion leaves `_test_products` behind in the shared database
findings.evidence: In the added 'queries real tables with rows' test the setup uses try/finally around `rawClient`, but the cleanup client (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _test_products`) runs after the `expect(sheetRows).toEqual(...)` assertions with no try/finally protecting it. If any assertion throws, the table (and its rows) persists in the app's own DATABASE_URL database, leaking state into subsequent tests/runs.

findings.summary: Connection leak: `rawClient.end()` is skipped if the DROP inside the finally block throws
findings.evidence: `} finally { await rawClient.query(`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ${table}`); await rawClient.end(); }` — the awaited DROP is not itself guarded, so any error from it (e.g. the connection already died mid-loop, or a lock) propagates out of the finally and `rawClient.end()` never executes, leaking an open pg connection for the rest of the suite.

findings.summary: Custom type parser ignores the `format` argument, so binary-format date/timestamp values would be returned as raw Buffers
findings.evidence: `datasourceTypeParser = (oid, format) => RAW_TEXT_OIDS.has(oid) ? (value: string) => value : getDefaultParser(oid, format)` — the identity branch is returned for both 'text' and 'binary' formats. pg's TypeOverrides.getTypeParser is called with the wire format; if a binary result ever reaches this client the identity parser hands back the raw Buffer typed as string, and `toCell` would then emit `{"type":"Buffer",...}` instead of a date. Guarding the identity branch with `format !== 'binary'` would be safer.

findings.summary: `toCell` can throw on non-serializable objects, aborting the whole grid load
findings.evidence: `if (typeof val === 'object' && val !== null) return JSON.stringify(val);` — JSON.stringify throws a TypeError on values containing BigInt or circular references. It is called inside `loadQueryResults`'s row loop (line 73), so a single bad value throws out of `loadQueryResults`, leaving `this.grid` partially populated and the index un-rebuilt (rebuildIndex on line 77 never runs), i.e. the view is left in an inconsistent state rather than showing a degraded cell.

findings.summary: Assertions weakened to `String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')`, which no longer distinguishes number 1 from string '1'
findings.evidence: The existing assertion `expect(queryResult.rows).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])` was replaced by `expect(String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')`. Since the change is specifically about how pg parses values into JS types, wrapping in String() removes the ability of this test to detect a parser regression (int4 silently becoming a string, or vice versa) — the very thing the new `types` option affects.

findings.summary: Duplicated test `queries real tables with rows` — the diff adds a second copy with weaker assertions while the original remains
findings.evidence: `it('queries real tables with rows')` now exists twice in the same describe block: the added copy at lines 114-197 (asserts via `toCell`/`String()`) and the pre-existing one at lines 309-391 (asserts `rows` toEqual `[{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }, ...]`). Jest runs both, so the suite now creates/drops `_test_products` twice and reports two identically-named results. The added copy adds no coverage over the original and actually asserts less precisely (String()/toCell coercion hides the raw value types the PR changes); it looks like an unintended duplication of a test the author meant to replace.

findings.summary: Assertions weakened to `String(rows[0].n)` — passes whether the driver returns a number or a string, so it can no longer detect parser regressions
findings.evidence: Previously `expect(queryResult.rows).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])`; now `expect(String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')` (also at line 111 and line 163 for `table_name`). Since the PR's whole subject is which pg OIDs get custom (raw-text) parsers, coercing every value through `String()` makes these tests insensitive to exactly the class of change being made — a wrong parser for int4/text would still produce '1'/'_test_products'.

findings.summary: `converts query runtime failures to bad request` now throws on the new `SET TimeZone` setup query, not on the user query — it passes for the wrong reason
findings.evidence: The mock only short-circuits `sql.startsWith('SET statement_timeout')`; the newly added `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` and `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` calls fall into the default branch which throws `syntax error at or near "FROM"`. So execution never reaches the wrapped user query, and the test would still pass even if the error mapping around the actual `SELECT` were removed. The mock should whitelist all `SET ` statements so the failure is injected on the query under test.

findings.summary: New exported `toCell` has no test in packages/sheets; its `Date → toISOString()` branch is exercised nowhere
findings.evidence: `toCell` is added and exported from packages/sheets (src/index.ts:197) but no sheets test file references it or ReadOnlyStore: grep for `toCell|ReadOnlyStore|loadQueryResults` matches only src files, the backend e2e, and docs — none of the ~60 files under packages/sheets/test or src/**/__tests__. Furthermore, because the service change makes pg return date/time values as raw strings, the `val instanceof Date` branch cannot be reached by the backend e2e either, so that branch is dead as far as any test is concerned. A few table-driven vitest cases (Date, plain object, Buffer, null-adjacent values) in packages/sheets would cover it cheaply.

findings.summary: Type-matrix loop gives no per-case labelling, so a failure won't identify the type
findings.evidence: The 40+ entry `typeMap` is iterated inside one `it(...)`; on failure Jest reports only 'check correct cell values for all pg built-in types' with an anonymous `expect(toCell(rows[0].val)).toBe(...)`. findings.summary: Existing unit test's pg mock no longer exercises the path it claims: it throws for anything not starting with `SET statement_timeout`, so the new `SET TimeZone` call now triggers the failure instead of the user query
findings.evidence: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.spec.ts:153-159 — `client.query.mockImplementation` returns a result only for `SET statement_timeout` and throws `syntax error at or near "FROM"` otherwise. With the two new session-setting queries added in `datasource.service.ts:144-145`, the throw now happens on `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'`, before the wrapped SELECT is ever issued. findings.summary: The pre-existing `queries real tables with rows` e2e test was left in place while a near-identical copy was added, producing two same-named tests that both create/TRUNCATE/DROP `_test_products`
findings.evidence: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:309 declares `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` again (the new copy is at :114). Both build and drop the same `_test_products` table in the same database; the old copy still asserts the raw row shape (`{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }` at :370-374) rather than the new `toCell` shape, so the two encode different expectations of the same contract, and any future value/format change must be fixed in two places.

findings.summary: Timestamp/timestamptz values now arrive as raw Postgres text (`2025-06-15 05:30:00+00`), a form the sheets date formatter's structured branches do not match, so date-formatted datasource cells silently lose the time component
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:24 and :40-42 only match `YYYY-MM-DD` and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`; a timestamptz string with a `+00` offset falls through to `new Date(value)` at :62 which returns `hasTime: false`, so `safeFormatDate` (:79-81) renders date-only. Before this change the backend returned a JS `Date`, which serialized to an ISO `T`-separated string over HTTP — a different (also unmatched, but differently rendered) input. No consumer of `ReadOnlyStore` was updated for the new textual form.

findings.summary: Design doc's Query Execution contract still describes only statement/connection timeouts and row limits; it does not record the new per-connection `SET TimeZone`/`SET DateStyle` session state or the raw-text date type parsing that now defines the response value format
findings.evidence: docs/design/sheets/datasource.md:156-162 lists wrapping, timeouts, max rows and response fields with no mention of UTC normalisation or that DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ are returned as Postgres text rather than JS Dates; likewise docs/design/backend.md:171 for `POST /datasources/:id/query`.

findings.summary: The new e2e test duplicates an existing test verbatim (same `it` name, same table, same setup)
findings.evidence: `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` now exists twice in the same describe block: the newly added copy at line 114 (asserting via `toCell`) and the pre-existing one at line 309 (asserting raw `rows` shape). Both create/truncate/drop the same `_test_products` table in the same database, so they duplicate work and can interfere; the author almost certainly meant to REPLACE the old test rather than add a near-copy next to it. Duplicated names also make failures ambiguous in reporting.

findings.summary: Generic value-stringification helper placed inside the ReadOnlyStore module and promoted to the sheets public API mainly for a backend test
findings.evidence: `toCell` is a generic unknown→string formatter with no dependency on ReadOnlyStore state, yet it lives in `store/readonly.ts` and is re-exported from `packages/sheets/src/index.ts` (line 197). Its only consumer outside the store is `packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts`. Repo convention is that cross-package shared helpers live in `@wafflebase/core` (or at least a util module); widening the sheets public API surface for a test assertion is avoidable scope.

findings.summary: `toCell` renders non-plain objects (Buffer, interval, circle) as raw JSON in cells, a user-visible representation choice the design doc does not sanction
findings.evidence: `JSON.stringify(val)` yields cell text such as `{"type":"Buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}` for BYTEA and `{"years":1,"months":2,"days":3}` for INTERVAL (asserted in the new e2e table at lines 219 and 254). The datasource design doc only states values are displayed as strings; internal pg-js object shapes leaking into spreadsheet cells is an approach decision worth an explicit design note or a friendlier rendering.

findings.summary: `val instanceof Date` branch in `toCell` is now unreachable for the datasource path it was written for
findings.evidence: The backend now forces DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ to raw text via `RAW_TEXT_OIDS`, so query rows no longer contain JS `Date` values; the Date branch is dead for the only production caller (`loadQueryResults`). Harmless but signals the two halves of the change were designed independently.

findings.summary: Datasource TLS connections disable certificate verification (`rejectUnauthorized: false`)
findings.evidence: `createClient` — the exact object literal this diff modifies (the new `types:` option is added at line 204) — builds every pg Client with `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false`. The decrypted datasource password (line 201, from `decrypt(ds.password)`) plus all query results travel over a TLS channel that accepts any certificate, including a self-signed one. An attacker positioned between the backend and the customer database (or able to spoof DNS/route for `ds.host`, which is fully user-controlled) terminates the connection, harvests the plaintext DB credentials, and returns arbitrary rows to the sheet. Enabling SSL in the UI gives users a false sense of protection. Pre-existing line, but it is the config object this change edits.

findings.summary: User SQL is string-interpolated into the executed statement and gated only by a keyword blacklist, permitting server file reads / SSRF / non-blacklisted DDL-free abuse
findings.evidence: `executeQuery` (modified in this diff — the SET statements at 143-145 were added directly above) passes the raw request body straight through: `const wrappedQuery = 'SELECT * FROM (' + dto.query + ') AS _q LIMIT ...'` (line 148). The only gate is `validateSelectQuery` (packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts:1-70), a regex blacklist of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/TRUNCATE/GRANT/REVOKE/EXEC/EXECUTE. Payloads that are literally `SELECT` but not read-only-safe pass unchanged: `SELECT pg_read_file('/etc/passwd')`, `SELECT pg_ls_dir('/')`, `SELECT lo_import('/etc/shadow')`, `SELECT * FROM dblink('host=169.254.169.254 port=80 ...','SELECT 1') AS t(x text)` (SSRF from the DB host), `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity` (DoS on the target DB). Any authenticated workspace member — including one who did not configure the datasource and does not know its credentials — reaches this via POST /datasources/:id/query (datasource.controller.ts:133-145), so a low-privileged member escalates to file read / lateral movement using an admin-configured connection. Pre-existing validator, but this diff extends the code path it guards.

findings.summary: Multi-statement detection strips string literals with a naive regex whose quote pairing differs from Postgres (E'' escapes, dollar quoting), so statement stacking may be possible
findings.evidence: The 'multiple statements' check runs on `withoutComments.replace(/'[^']*'/g, '')` (line 60) and then splits on ';'. That pairing disagrees with Postgres for backslash-escaped quotes in E-strings (`E'\''` — pg sees one string, the regex sees `'\'` and leaves a dangling quote that then swallows following text, semicolons included) and for dollar-quoted bodies (`$$...$$`), which the regex does not model at all. Because the executed text is the ORIGINAL `dto.query` (datasource.service.ts:148), any pairing mismatch that hides a ';' from the validator yields real statement stacking over pg's simple-query protocol. The keyword blacklist does not contain COPY, SET, CALL, DO, VACUUM or REFRESH, so a stacked `COPY t FROM PROGRAM '...'` (command execution on the DB host when the role is superuser) or `SET ROLE ...` needs no blacklisted word. I could not finish a payload that both parses in pg inside the `SELECT * FROM (...) AS _q` wrapper and evades the split, hence low confidence; the parser mismatch itself is demonstrable.

findings.summary: SSRF / internal port scanning: datasource host and port are unvalidated and the backend dials them on demand
findings.evidence: `createClient` (line 196, the method whose config this diff edits) connects to `ds.host`/`ds.port` with no allow-list, no private/link-local address rejection and no DNS-rebinding protection; CreateDataSourceDto only enforces `@Length(1,253)` on host and 1..65535 on port (packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.dto.ts:17-25). Any authenticated user POSTs a datasource for `169.254.169.254:80`, `127.0.0.1:6379`, or any internal host, then calls POST /datasources/:id/test (controller line 120). `testConnection` returns `{ success:false, error: (error as Error).message }` verbatim (datasource.service.ts:121), so 'ECONNREFUSED' vs. connection-timeout vs. a protocol error is a reliable oracle for mapping the internal network from outside. Pre-existing, but it is the connection factory this change modifies.

findings.summary: Raw Postgres error text is returned to the API client
findings.evidence: `throw new BadRequestException(pgError.message || 'Query execution failed')` (line 169, in the executeQuery body this diff edits) forwards the driver's message untouched. Postgres errors routinely disclose schema names, column names, file paths, role names and server version fragments; combined with the unvalidated query path above this turns failed queries into a schema-enumeration channel for any workspace member. `testConnection` (line 121) leaks the same way, including authentication-failure detail for probed hosts.

findings.summary: New integration tests run CREATE/TRUNCATE/DROP TABLE against whatever database DATABASE_URL points at
findings.evidence: The added tests build a raw pg Client from `parseDatabaseUrl(process.env.DATABASE_URL!)` and execute `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _test_products`, `TRUNCATE _test_products RESTART IDENTITY`, `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _test_products`, and in the type-matrix test a loop of `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ${table}` / `CREATE TABLE ${table} (val ${sqlType})`. packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:67 only does `process.env.DATABASE_URL ??= DEFAULT_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so an already-set DATABASE_URL (a developer shell pointing at a staging/production database) is used as-is and the suite performs destructive DDL there with the application's real credentials. The table name is also interpolated into DDL, so the pattern generalises badly.
